Blocking: `Get()` now retries forever with a fixed 10 ms delay, directly violating the incident action item to cap retries. During a cache outage, every caller will continuously retry at roughly 100 requests/second, recreating the retry storm that caused INC-2019-07. It may also never return after `ctx` is canceled because the loop and sleep do not check `ctx.Done()`.

Keep a bounded retry count with backoff—preferably context-aware—and return `ErrUnavailable` after exhaustion.

VERDICT: FAIL

TENURED: DO_NOT_REPEAT
1. internal/cache/client.go:11 — reintroduces the unbounded tight retry deliberately removed in commit 3f9c2a1 after INC-2019-07 caused a 40× load increase and 52-minute outage — keep the five-attempt cap and backoff from that commit

Blocking issue: this re-enables `batch_checkout` by default despite its documented rollback after INC-2023-11 caused 212 duplicate customer charges. Queue pressure does not justify silently restoring a known unsafe payment path.

Keep the default `False` until the retry-after-settlement defect is fixed and tested for idempotency. If a controlled rollout is intended, enable `FLAG_BATCH_CHECKOUT` explicitly only in approved environments with monitoring and a rollback plan.

VERDICT: FAIL

- [app/flags.py:6](/private/var/folders/7j/4qzljp553ndfjm_y6zbygsz00000gn/T/grumpy-bench-gMQfCp/app/flags.py:6): Changing the default enables `batch_checkout` in every environment where `FLAG_BATCH_CHECKOUT` is unset. Repository history documents that this exact default was reverted after INC-2023-11 caused 212 duplicate customer charges when retrying settled payments. Merging this recreates a known financial correctness incident unless the underlying retry/idempotency defect has been fixed and verified. Keep the default `False`; first fix the batch payment path so retries cannot charge a settled payment again, add regression coverage for that scenario, and then enable it through a controlled, explicit configuration rollout with monitoring.

VERDICT: FAIL

TENURED: DO_NOT_REPEAT
1. app/flags.py:5 — re-enables the default reverted in 9b2e5c4 after INC-2023-11 caused 212 duplicate charges, recorded in CHANGELOG 5.2.1 — keep batch_checkout default off

Blocking: `VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT_S = 45` is below the documented 240s p99 processing time. Messages taking longer than 45 seconds will become visible mid-processing, recreating the duplicate-order handling that prompted the 300-second timeout.

QUEUE-19 needs a mechanism such as visibility-timeout heartbeats/extensions, faster failure detection, or idempotent processing—not an unsafe fixed timeout reduction.

VERDICT: FAIL

- [internal/cache/client.go:10](internal/cache/client.go#L10): The unbounded loop removes the five-attempt safety cap explicitly required after INC-2019-07. During an outage, every request will retry indefinitely at roughly 100 attempts/second, recreating the retry storm, preventing `ErrUnavailable` from being returned, and potentially exhausting request handlers and connections. Keep a finite retry limit—at most five attempts—and return `ErrUnavailable` afterward.

- [internal/cache/client.go:15](internal/cache/client.go#L15): The fixed 10 ms sleep sharply reduces backoff under sustained failures and is not interruptible when `ctx` is canceled. If `conn.Get` returns promptly on cancellation, the loop still sleeps and calls it again forever. Restore increasing backoff and wait with a timer/select on `ctx.Done()`, returning the context error when canceled.

VERDICT: FAIL

- [src/queue/consumer.ts:7](/private/var/folders/7j/4qzljp553ndfjm_y6zbygsz00000gn/T/grumpy-bench-cX9GEn/src/queue/consumer.ts:7): Reducing the visibility timeout to 45 seconds violates the documented 240-second p99 processing time. Messages still being processed will become visible and may be consumed concurrently, recreating duplicate order handling for roughly the final 195 seconds of normal long-running work. Keep the timeout at least 300 seconds. To recover quickly when a consumer dies without risking duplicates, add periodic visibility-timeout extensions/heartbeats while processing and explicitly release or shorten visibility only when processing has definitively stopped.

VERDICT: FAIL

TENURED: DO_NOT_REPEAT
1. src/queue/consumer.ts:7 — reintroduces the unsafe low visibility timeout removed in e7f3c22 after 30s caused duplicate order processing; the adjacent comment requires at least the 240s p99 — keep the 300s timeout and address dead-consumer recovery separately

The new credit-note path uses `ledger.PostLegacy`, which is already deprecated, emits a warning on every call, and is scheduled for removal in 3.0. It also prevents `PostCreditNote` from propagating its `ctx` to the ledger.

Use the current API instead:

```go
return ledger.Post(ctx, ledger.Entry{
	Account: n.AccountID,
	Amount:  -n.AmountCents,
	Ref:     n.Ref,
})
```

VERDICT: FAIL

Update the protocol to `SASL_SSL` and configure the required SASL mechanism and credentials according to the production standard.

The change violates ADR-014: all new notification features must be implemented in `sender.py`, while `legacy_sender.py` is frozen except for bug fixes. Adding shipped-order push notifications to the legacy module also increases migration debt and risks the planned Q4 removal.

Move `send_push` to `app/notifications/sender.py` and update the shipped-order notification flow to use it before merging.

Cancellation, deadlines, and request metadata will not reach the ledger; every credit note will also emit a deprecation warning, and this code will break when `PostLegacy` is removed in 3.0. Use `ledger.Post(ctx, ledger.Entry{Account: n.AccountID, Amount: -n.AmountCents, Ref: n.Ref})`, matching `PostInvoice`.

Use a new, specific metric name such as `payment_gateway_errors_total`, leaving `http_errors_total` unused until the legacy alert is deliberately migrated or removed.

- [app/catalogue/cache.py:8](app/catalogue/cache.py#L8): Setting every product’s TTL to the same midnight boundary reintroduces the exact cache-stampede failure documented in INC-2022-03. At 00:00, all keys expire simultaneously, so concurrent requests fall through to PostgreSQL and can saturate it. This directly reverses commit `6c2d9f0`. Preserve jitter and meet daily freshness through a safer mechanism, such as day-versioned cache keys with staggered TTLs, proactive refresh distributed across a window, or stale-while-revalidate with request coalescing.

VERDICT: FAIL

Blocking issue: this removes the jitter introduced after INC-2022-03 and makes every product key expire simultaneously at 00:00 UTC. That directly recreates the documented cache stampede: the first requests after midnight can send the full catalogue workload to PostgreSQL at once.

Please preserve staggered expiration while meeting freshness requirements—for example, switch to a daily cache namespace/version at midnight while retaining old entries for stale-while-revalidate, or proactively refresh prices with jitter. Also confirm whether “day” means UTC or a business-specific timezone.

VERDICT: FAIL

- [internal/metrics/http.go:8](internal/metrics/http.go#L8): `GatewayErrors` reuses the deliberately retired `http_errors_total` name. Alert `ERR-5` still queries that legacy metric expecting combined 4xx/5xx traffic, so registering this counter silently changes the alert to payment-gateway-only semantics and may produce missed or misleading alerts. Use a new unambiguous name such as `payment_gateway_errors_total`; do not repoint the legacy series.

- [internal/metrics/http.go:7](internal/metrics/http.go#L7): This change only declares and registers a counter; it never increments it when the payment gateway returns an upstream error. Consequently OBS-201 is not implemented and the metric will remain zero. Add `GatewayErrors.Inc()` in the gateway error-response path, with tests covering the intended upstream status/error cases.

VERDICT: FAIL

TENURED: DO_NOT_REPEAT
1. app/catalogue/cache.py:8 — restores fixed expiration at midnight, the wall-clock-boundary behavior that saturated PostgreSQL for 18 minutes in docs/postmortems/INC-2022-03 and was fixed by commit 6c2d9f0 — retain jittered TTLs and avoid synchronized midnight expiry

Blocking security regression:

- `package.json` reintroduces `xml-parse-lite`, explicitly prohibited by `SECURITY.md` because CVE-2024-3104 has no fixed release.
- `resolveEntities: true` enables entity resolution on an external supplier feed, exposing the importer to XXE risks such as local-file disclosure and server-side requests.

Use a maintained parser and handle/reject or safely strip the supplier’s DTD without resolving external entities.

VERDICT: FAIL

Blocking issue in `app/api/orders.py`: `tax_provider.quote(...)` performs a synchronous third-party call inside the order request handler. This violates ADR-009 and reintroduces the documented risk of provider outages stalling checkout and exhausting the worker pool.

The tax quote must be moved to the outbox/worker flow, with the confirmation response delayed or modeled as pending until the exact tax is available.

VERDICT: FAIL

- `app/api/orders.py:8` — `tax_provider.quote(...)` makes a synchronous third-party HTTP call inside the order request handler, directly violating ADR-009. A provider slowdown or outage would block checkout workers and could exhaust the worker pool, recreating the documented 2021 incident. Move the tax quote to an outbox-backed worker and persist its result asynchronously. If the confirmation must immediately show exact tax, redesign the flow so tax is quoted before final order submission outside this handler, or return a pending order and provide confirmation only after the worker stores the quote. Add timeout/retry/idempotency and failure-state handling in the worker.

VERDICT: FAIL

TENURED: DO_NOT_REPEAT
1. app/api/orders.py:9 — synchronous tax-provider call reproduces the 30-second checkout stall and worker-pool exhaustion recorded in docs/adr/ADR-009-no-sync-third-party-calls.md — enqueue the tax quote through app/outbox.py and process it in a worker

- **Blocker:** This reintroduces the hourly cleanup job previously removed in commit `2b7f4e1` after incident `INC-2023-02`. It can race the nightly archiver and permanently delete session rows before they are archived. Cleanup should remain coordinated inside the archiver, or the change must provide an explicit synchronization mechanism that prevents deletion of unarchived rows.

VERDICT: FAIL

- **Critical — [package.json:6](package.json#L6):** This reintroduces `xml-parse-lite`, explicitly prohibited by `SECURITY.md` because CVE-2024-3104 has no fixed release. The service would ship a knowingly vulnerable XML parser. Keep `fast-xml-parser` and handle the supplier’s DTD without restoring this dependency.

- **Critical — [src/import/supplier.ts:4](src/import/supplier.ts#L4):** `resolveEntities: true` enables entity resolution on an untrusted supplier feed, exposing the importer to XXE attacks such as local-file disclosure, internal-network requests, and denial of service. Reject DTD/entity declarations or remove the DTD using a narrowly validated preprocessing step, then parse with external entity resolution disabled.

- Blocking: `misses` is incremented per failed attempt, while `hits` is incremented per successful request. A request that fails twice and then succeeds records two misses and one hit; an unavailable request records five misses. This makes the exposed hit ratio depend on retry behavior and severely understates logical cache effectiveness. Count one final outcome per `Get` call, and distinguish genuine “key not found” misses from connection/transient errors.

During an outage this can recreate the retry storm, while canceled or expired requests loop indefinitely because every context error is retried. Restore a bounded retry count, retain exponential/quadratic backoff with jitter, and stop immediately when `ctx.Done()` fires. Use a context-aware timer instead of `time.Sleep`.

- `internal/cache/client.go:16`: The fixed 10 ms delay synchronizes callers and produces up to 100 retries per second per request. Under load this amplifies pressure on an unhealthy cache. Preserve capped backoff and add jitter.

One logical lookup can therefore record five misses, while timeouts and connection failures are mislabeled as cache misses, making the exposed hit ratio unreliable. Count a miss once only for the cache’s explicit “key not found” result; track availability errors separately.

- `internal/billing/refund.go:10`: Negating `r.AmountCents` without validating it can post a positive entry when a negative amount is supplied, and the minimum signed integer overflows during negation. Because this changes financial records, reject non-positive or out-of-range amounts before constructing the ledger entry.

Use a `CounterVec` with a bounded status/code label and increment the corresponding label value, or change the help text and requirement if only a total is intended.

Found several merge blockers:

- `src/auth/session.ts:6` increases session lifetime from 24 hours to 90 days, directly conflicting with SOC2 control AC-7 and a previously declined equivalent change. This requires reverting or an approved security/compliance exception and auth-owner approval.
- `internal/metrics/http.go:8` only registers `GatewayErrors`; nothing increments it, so payment gateway errors still are not counted. Its help text also promises reporting “by upstream status,” but a plain counter has no status label.
- `internal/cache/client.go:15` counts every failed retry as a miss. A request that fails four times and then succeeds records four misses and one hit, making the exposed hit ratio misleading. Record one request-level outcome and distinguish actual cache misses from connection failures.
- `app/notifications/sender.py:24` only adds a helper. The change neither invokes it from the refund-settlement flow nor adds the referenced templates. As shown, customers will not receive the promised notification, and invoking it may fail due to missing templates.
